old: D-Xylose (right, left, right) would require old C2 to keep its configuration as the new C2. Old C2 becomes the aldehyde carbon and loses its stereocenter.
new: D-Xylose (right, left, right) does not match the surviving centers. Old C2 becomes the aldehyde carbon, and old C3, C4 and C5 read left, left, right.
why: Old x1 claimed xylose = galactose with old C2 kept, but galactose old C2,C3,C4 read right, left, left, not xylose's right, left, right.

old: Like simple amides and 2-pyridone, thymine strongly prefers the lactam (diketo) tautomer A, with two C=O groups and two N–H groups. The C=O bond and amide resonance make it far more stable than the lactim (enol-like) forms. In the A·T pair, thymine N3–H donates to adenine N1, and thymine C4=O accepts from adenine's 6-NH2. The rare enol tautomers change the donor/acceptor pattern and can cause mispairing (with G).
